steps.body: Time breaks the pattern of tens: an hour holds 60 minutes and a minute holds 60 seconds, but the two decisions are unchanged.
steps.narration: Time breaks the pattern of tens: an hour holds 60 minutes and a minute holds 60 seconds, but the two decisions are unchanged.

widget.prompt: How many minutes in 3 hours? Hop one hour at a time.

commonLandings.feedback: Two hops reach 120 minutes; the hike lasts three hours.
Four hops overshoot — three hours is 180 minutes.

widget.missFeedback: Each hour is 60 minutes, so three reach 180.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — each hour is 60 minutes, so three reach 180.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — three hours stops exactly at 180 minutes.

predict.prompt: Does a factor of 60 change the method?
predict.reveal: Direction and factor are all a conversion ever needs; 60 simply replaces 100 or 1,000.

cml.actionGoal: Convert hours, minutes, and seconds using the correct factor of 60.
invariants: One hour is 60 minutes and one minute is 60 seconds.
misconceptions: Applying a metric factor of 100 or 1,000 to time.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: A rest stop measures 4 minutes, and each minute is 60 seconds. Compute 4 × 60.

commonErrors.feedback: Adding mixes a quantity with a rate. Each of the 4 minutes contributes 60 seconds, so they multiply.
That divided. Going to the SMALLER unit needs more of them, so the number must grow.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the quantity and the conversion factor, then decide whether the count should grow or shrink.

widget.prompt: Apply the time relationship to a new value: how many minutes are in 4 hours?

commonLandings.feedback: Three hops represent three hours; four hours needs one more hop.
Five hops overshoot; four hours is 240 minutes.

widget.missFeedback: Four equal hops of 60 minutes land at 240 minutes.
widget.successFeedback: 240 minutes — four hour-hops of 60 minutes each.
widget.lowFeedback: This landing is short of four complete hour-hops.
widget.highFeedback: This landing is past four complete hour-hops.

widget.prompt: Apply without the opening model: A hike measures 180 minutes, and each hour is 60 minutes. Compute 180 ÷ 60.

commonErrors.feedback: 180 is the count in minutes. Switching to the bigger hour must make the NUMBER smaller.
That multiplied. Going to the BIGGER unit needs fewer of them, so divide.

widget.prompt: Diagnose a time conversion: how should 5 hours be converted to minutes?

options.label: Multiply by 60 to get 300 minutes
options.feedback: Correct — each of the five hours contains 60 minutes.

options.label: Divide by 60 to get 1/12 minute
options.feedback: Minutes are smaller than hours, so the numerical count must grow, not shrink.

options.label: Keep the number 5 because time is unchanged
options.feedback: The duration stays fixed, but changing the unit changes its numerical measure.

options.label: Multiply by 100 to get 500 minutes
options.feedback: Time uses 60 minutes per hour, not a metric factor of 100.

widget.prompt: A workout lasts 180 seconds, and each minute is 60 seconds. Compute 180 ÷ 60.

commonErrors.feedback: That multiplied. Minutes are the BIGGER unit, so fewer of them are needed — divide instead.
Subtracting one minute's worth of seconds does not convert units; the whole count divides by 60.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Decide whether the target unit is bigger or smaller, then multiply or divide by the stated factor.
